quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: If you are under 21 and convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol, your license will be suspended for how long on a first offense?

options.text: 60 days
30 days
Six months
One year

questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 convicted of driving under the influence face penalties for high blood alcohol concentration (BAC), regardless of their actual BAC level. The penalty for a first offense is a 12-month license suspension.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashing lights.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means drivers next to it may pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you be most concerned about when you see this sign?

options.text: Your headlights will be out of alignment because one side of your car is higher.
You may damage a tire if you drift onto the shoulder.
You may hydroplane if the shoulder has water on it.
You may lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When may you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: You should use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: If you are under 21, at what blood alcohol level are you considered to be driving under the influence?

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.10 percent or higher.
0.05 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.

questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot legally drive with any measurable alcohol in their system. You are considered to be driving under the influence if your blood alcohol level is 0.02 percent or higher.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Speed up above traffic speed to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Highway entrance ramps often have acceleration lanes. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely into an opening.

questions.question: What should you do if there are two railroad tracks next to each other?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing.
After one train passes, check for a second train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check for a second train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is approaching on either track.

questions.question: On two-lane, two-way streets or highways, where should you start a left turn?

options.text: Close to the centerline.
Close to the outside line.
In the right lane.
From any lane.

questions.explanation: On two-lane, two-way streets or highways, start left turns as close to the centerline as possible.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead turns sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means stop. Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing the lanes. You may cross these lines:

options.text: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
To pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Never, under any circumstances.
Only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.explanation: Honk to alert the other driver. If they do not move, steer right. Do not steer left because if the other driver swerves at the last moment, you will still crash. Brake firmly to reduce the impact.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and go carefully.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It increases.
It decreases.
It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. At higher speeds, stay extra alert for hazards.

questions.question: If you are arrested for driving under the influence and refuse a blood test, what happens?

options.text: You must attend drug counseling.
You spend one day in jail.
Your driver license is suspended.
You pay a $300 fine.

questions.explanation: If you refuse a breath, blood, or urine test after a DUI arrest, your driving privilege is automatically suspended for one year.
